claim: The patch does not enable analysis of types for which source generation is suppressed. Every code edit occurs inside member-key collection, after collection and diagnosis of the type must already have begun; none changes the earlier SuppressSourceGeneration decision that caused these types to be skipped. Consequently the reported loss of MsgPack003/MsgPack004/MsgPack005 and other contract diagnostics remains, despite the new README claim that these types are validated.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.SuppressedTypeIsAnalyzedWithoutGeneratingSource from tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.cs. The run for a suppressed type with a public property lacking [Key] or [IgnoreMember] must contain MsgPack004 while the valid suppressed-type run produces no generated trees. On the unfixed head the MsgPack004 assertion fails because no diagnostic is reported.

claim: The README incorrectly excludes MsgPack017 as an AOT-only check. Its triggering behaviour—deserialization replacing an init-property initializer's value with the type's default—also applies when the suppressed type is serialized through the dynamic resolvers. Such a type therefore still violates MsgPack017 and should receive the diagnostic under the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Run SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerReceiptTests.InitInitializerWarningIsReportedForSuppressedType from the generated receipt test file. A [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type with a keyed init property initialized to 42 must produce MsgPack017; the implementation described by the README produces none.

claim: The new duplicate-key guards silently discard every member after the first with the same integer or string key, without reporting MsgPack007. For example, a [MessagePackObject] with two properties both annotated [Key(0)] now gets through TypeCollector without the duplicate-key diagnostic from the generator/collector path (the path relied on when source generation is suppressed). Two [Key("same")] properties have the same problem. Avoiding the Dictionary.Add exception must not turn the invalid object into a silently accepted one.

receipt_plan.detail: Run DuplicateKeyDiagnosticsReceiptTests.DuplicateKeysAreReported for both integer and string keys. It drives MessagePackGenerator over a MessagePackObject containing duplicate keys and asserts that the generator run contains MsgPack007; on head the guards drop the duplicate and the assertion fails.

claim: The change classifies MsgPack017 as source-generation-only and suppresses it for types using dynamic serialization, but MsgPack017 describes a runtime deserialization hazard: an init property initializer is replaced by the type's default value. That hazard still applies when no formatter is generated, so suppressed types lose a relevant contract warning and the README gives users incorrect guidance.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] with a [Key] init property that has an initializer and expect MsgPack017. This follows the runtime behavior recorded in [L6] and doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md; the current SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed test instead locks in the missing warning.
